review: 1:1–3 is a three-line opening stanza against the print's four-line tune 76.76.88 – 66.99 (the same class as tr0211); it is kept short rather than padded, so the abbreviated cry 'O the greatness of the Beloved's grace' stands alone.
2:2 בְּרוּחוֹ נִחַנִי — the Arabic بِرُوحِهِ هَدَانِي is 'by His Spirit He guided me'; נָחָה is the Exodus verb (Exod 13:21, נֹחֶה), so guidance is the wilderness-leading and not mere advice.

3:2 וְחִבֵּשׁ פְּצָעָי — the Arabic وَضَمَّدَ الْجِرَاح is 'He bound up the wounds'; חָבַשׁ is the biblical verb of Isa 61:1 (לַחֲבֹשׁ לְנִשְׁבְּרֵי־לֵב) and Ps 147:3, and the same verse supplies the 'healing' of the first clause.

3:2 בַּחֲבוּרָתוֹ — the Arabic بِحُبْرِهِ is the print's spelling of بِحُبُرِهِ 'with His stripes' (Isa 53:5, וּבַחֲבֻרָתוֹ נִרְפָּא־לָנוּ); the Hebrew therefore quotes the Isaiah noun directly, which also explains why the wound-healing follows in the same line.

4:4 לֹא־יַסְפִּיק שֶׁבַח הַנִּפְדֶּה — the Arabic لَا يَكْفِي سُبْحُ الْمُفْتَدِي is 'the praise of the ransomed does not suffice'; the singular is kept as a collective, so the line speaks of the ransomed person generically rather than of 'our praise'.
